reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that cognition operates through reinforcement mechanisms where thoughts interact via associative memory. Pleasure and pain act as binary switches influencing action repetition or cessation. These dynamics form a dualistic feedback system: positive reinforcement encourages behavior continuation while negative reinforcement halts it. This aligns with classical conditioning models but extends into higher-order cognitive domains. The vis-a-tergo principle introduces non-conscious causality—emotional expressions emerge directly from stimulus-response pathways rather than deliberative thought. Thus, the three primitives define a triadic structure: cognitive reinforcement (thoughts), hedonic modulation (pleasure-pain), and instinctive drive (vis-a-tergo). Each layer interacts through shared variables like valence and neural response, forming a hierarchical yet interdependent model of behavior generation.
